title: Certificate of Good Standing in Saskatchewan: How to Get It
h1: How to Get a Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Status) in Saskatchewan
description: Saskatchewan calls it a Certificate of Status. The $15 ISC fee, every ordering route, and how CRS delivers yours in about 3 business hours, all-in.
body:
**Need proof your corporation is in good standing?** [Order your Saskatchewan Certificate of Status →](/order/good-standing?src=article-how-to-get-a-certificate-of-good-standing-in-saskatchewan) · {{price:good-standing}} + tax all-in, government fee included, delivered in about 3 business hours.

In Saskatchewan, the document everyone calls a certificate of good standing is officially a **Certificate of Status**, issued by the province's Corporate Registry — which is operated by ISC — for a **$15 government fee**. You can order it from ISC directly, or CRS retrieves it for **{{price:good-standing}} + tax all-in** in about 3 business hours, no ISC account or paper form needed. Here's what the certificate proves, what it costs through every route, and the one thing to check before you order — because a certificate for a corporation that isn't in good standing helps nobody.

## What is a certificate of good standing in Saskatchewan?

It's the registry's formal confirmation that your corporation exists and is active — not dissolved, struck or amalgamated — on Saskatchewan's Corporate Registry at the moment the certificate is issued. Saskatchewan's registry sells it under the name **Certificate of Status**: ISC's fee table lists no product called a "certificate of good standing," so the Certificate of Status is the document a bank, lawyer or another province's registry means when they ask for one. (The same naming quirk exists in [Alberta](/articles/how-to-get-a-certificate-of-good-standing-in-alberta) and [Ontario](/articles/certificate-of-status-ontario).)

For the general concept — what "good standing" means across Canada and what the certificate does and doesn't prove — see our guide to [certificates of good standing in Canada](/guides/what-is-a-certificate-of-good-standing-canada). The short version: it's a point-in-time snapshot, which is why whoever requested it usually wants one issued recently.

## When do you actually need one?

The requests nearly always come from someone else's compliance checklist. Banks ask for one before opening accounts or [advancing a business loan](/guides/certificate-of-good-standing-for-bank-loan). Lenders and investors ask during due diligence. Other provinces ask when a Saskatchewan corporation registers extra-provincially. Grant programs ask [before releasing funds](/guides/certificate-of-good-standing-for-grants). Buyers' lawyers ask in every share or asset sale.

What they're screening for is simple: that the corporation on the paperwork is alive and compliant at the registry. Which leads to the step most people skip.

## Check your corporation's status before you order

A Certificate of Status for a corporation that has fallen out of compliance is a problem discovered at the worst possible time — in front of the bank. Search your corporation first (the widget at the top of this page checks the registry free). If the company shows active, order the certificate. If something looks off, the usual culprit is an overdue annual return: Saskatchewan returns are due **one month after your incorporation anniversary**, the government fee is **$60 on time or $110 late**, and a corporation that keeps missing them is eventually struck from the registry. Our [Saskatchewan annual return guide](/articles/how-to-file-your-annual-return-in-saskatchewan) covers the fix; CRS files outstanding returns in 1 business day, then pulls the certificate once the record is clean.

## How much does a Saskatchewan Certificate of Status cost?

Under ISC's Corporate Registry fee table (effective April 15, 2026):

| Item | Government fee |
|---|---|
| Certificate of Status | $15 |
| Electronic certification (add-on) | $5 per document |
| Manual certification (add-on) | $40 per document |
| Document Order priority service | $75 per order |
| Corporate profile report (for comparison) | $10 |

Those are ISC's charges if you order directly. Through CRS the certificate is **{{price:good-standing}} + applicable tax, all-in** — government fee included — delivered as a PDF in about **3 business hours**. If you need the fuller picture of the corporation (directors, registered office, filing history) rather than just proof of standing, a [corporate profile report](/articles/corporate-profile-report-canada) is the better document; our [comparison guide](/guides/corporate-profile-report-vs-certificate-of-good-standing) covers which one a given gatekeeper actually wants.

## How do you order one from ISC directly?

Saskatchewan's registry runs through ISC's Corporate Registry application at corporateregistry.isc.ca — records from 1999 onward are searchable online there, and that's the self-serve starting point. The paper route is ISC's **Document Order form (COM4)**, which covers profile reports, Certificates of Status and document copies, submitted by mail or fax with a submission cover page; payment is by credit card over the phone, cheque, or an ISC account, and pre-1999 records can *only* be ordered this way. Standard orders are processed from the date ISC receives them; the **$75 priority service** moves a document order to "within one business day, where possible."

That works fine when you have the time. When the certificate is holding up a signing, CRS's route is faster: we pull the certificate from the registry on your behalf — no ISC registration, no form, no fax machine — and deliver it in about 3 business hours. [Order the Saskatchewan certificate here](/good-standing/saskatchewan-certificate-of-good-standing), or search your company in the widget above and order straight from the result.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a certificate of good standing the same as a certificate of status in Saskatchewan?

Yes. Saskatchewan's Corporate Registry, operated by ISC, officially sells the document as a Certificate of Status — its fee table has no product called a certificate of good standing. Banks, lawyers and other registries use the two names interchangeably, so if someone asks you for a certificate of good standing for a Saskatchewan corporation, the Certificate of Status is the document they mean.

### How much does a Saskatchewan Certificate of Status cost?

The government fee is $15 under ISC's Corporate Registry fee table effective April 15, 2026. Certification costs extra — $5 for electronic certification or $40 for manual — and ISC's priority document-order service is $75 per order. CRS supplies the certificate for {{price:good-standing}} + applicable tax all-in, including the government charges, in about 3 business hours.

### How long is a certificate of status valid?

It has no expiry date — it states the corporation's standing on the day it was issued. Whoever asked for it decides how fresh it must be, and banks and lawyers typically want one issued within the last 30 to 60 days. Order it close to when you need it, not months in advance.

### Why would a Saskatchewan corporation not be in good standing?

The usual reason is an overdue annual return. Saskatchewan annual returns are due one month after the incorporation anniversary, and a corporation that stops filing moves to non-compliance, then notice of dissolution, then is struck from the registry. Filing the outstanding return — $60 government fee, or $110 once late — restores compliance; a struck corporation needs revival first.

### Do I need an ISC account to get a certificate?

Not through CRS — we obtain the certificate from the Saskatchewan Corporate Registry on your behalf with no ISC registration, portal login or paper form on your side. Ordering directly from ISC yourself means using its Corporate Registry application online or submitting its Document Order form by mail or fax.
